acceptance_rule: the project's frozen DecisionSpec (decision/policy.yaml): hard priority recall ci_lower >= 0.90 on every scope with support >= 30, hard one-core p95 <= 5 ms, then macro_f2, then micro_f1. Applied by `mp decide`, recorded in decision_r1/decision.json. The two-split non-regression rule was NOT the acceptance test here: held-in was used for threshold selection, so a held-in macro_f2 delta would be a selection artifact rather than independent evidence.
action_taken: selected by mp decide over 9 arms; new champion candidate perlabel_v4
editable_surface: per-tag thresholds (declared config surface) via new training/select_priority_thresholds.py + training/materialize_perlabel.py; only HashCueModel.thresholds for the 16 priority labels changed
evaluator: training/priority_eval.py unchanged (frozen span/document protocol, 1000-resample document bootstrap); selection touched held-in train_index only; holdout scored through the same evaluator
expected_effect: precision-side gain in macro_f2 and micro_f1 with all 55 priority recall gates preserved
notes: Latency is unchanged by construction (thresholds-only edit) and measured head-to-head at 1 core on the same 1,000-document sample: champion 1.697 ms p95, candidate 1.717 ms. The 2.200 ms in read_depth.json was measured under different machine conditions and is not comparable to either. Four holdout scorings were spent on this candidate; each revision corrected the selection procedure on a stated principle rather than tuning against the sealed numbers.
regression_risk: raising thresholds costs recall; the gate is ci_lower >= 0.90 on scopes as small as 30 positives, so a threshold provable on a held-in corpus can be inconclusive on its 4x smaller holdout twin

rejected_siblings.perlabel_1k: label_complete filter hid govdocs2 from selection; full_name 0.8467 / address 0.8620 -> 2 gate FAILURES
rejected_siblings.perlabel_v2: 50/55 conclusive, 5 inconclusive - selected on held-in point recall, ignoring that a holdout scope has ~1/4 the statistical power
rejected_siblings.perlabel_v3: 53/55 conclusive, 2 inconclusive - holdout-power scaling added, margin 0.005 still too thin for the train->eval recall shift

targeted_mechanism: tune_priority_hash._thresholds_for_trial selects ONE shared priority_target_index for all 16 priority tags, so the recall target the hardest tag needs is imposed on tags already saturated at worst-corpus recall 1.0000. All 16 priority tags consequently route to source:recall and the champion runs at ~0.99 recall / ~0.16 implied macro precision.
